summary.headline: Nazara Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 803 crore (up 53% YoY) and EBITDA rose 93% to INR 120 crore, helped by Bluetile and BestPlay consolidation from 1 August 2026.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter including Bluetile and BestPlay, consolidated from 1 August 2026, and Nazara reported record revenue of INR 803 crore with EBITDA margin up 311 bps to 14.9%. Gaming is now 82% of revenue and effectively all EBITDA before corporate costs. Organic gaming growth was modest at 11% revenue and 17% EBITDA, with the acquired mobile businesses doing most of the lifting. Management, under a new CEO, CFO and Executive Director, framed the next year around platform centres of excellence, AI adoption and gaming focus, and declined to give numerical growth targets. Non-core assets (NODWIN, AdTech, Absolute Sports and others) are to be monetised opportunistically.

segments.name: Mobile gaming (incl. Bluetile and BestPlay)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 550 crore (up 167% YoY) and EBITDA INR 103 crore (up 151%). Bluetile and BestPlay contributed INR 329 crore revenue and INR 64 crore EBITDA in their first two months under Nazara; Aug-Sep margin was about 19.5% per the analyst, versus about 10.5% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Mobile studios (organic)
segments.commentary: WildWorks revenue up 41% and EBITDA up 39% on Animal Jam content. Kiddopia revenue up 21% with subscribers at 5% and ARPU at $7.94 (up 8%), but EBITDA fell on higher user acquisition. Fusebox revenue down 4% on lower organic installs while EBITDA rose 7%.

segments.name: PC and console (Curve)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 77 crore (up 27%) and EBITDA INR 30 crore (up 61%), margin 38.9% versus 30.8%. Drivers were Sovereign Tower, the mobile debut of Wobbly Life and Human: Fall Flat, which has passed 60 million players.

segments.name: Offline gaming (Funky Monkeys, SMAAASH)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat at INR 29 crore, EBITDA up 29% to INR 8 crore. Funky Monkeys opened 10 stores in the last 12 months and plans 5 more in FY27. SMAAASH 2.0 launch is slightly delayed pending regulatory approvals.

segments.name: AdTech (Datawrkz, Space & Time)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 124 crore and EBITDA INR 0.8 crore. Management expects a temporary H2 dip as an anchor client restructures and pauses ad spend.

segments.name: Sports and media (Absolute Sports, Pro Football Network, Sportskeeda)
segments.commentary: Absolute Sports revenue INR 23 crore with adjusted EBITDA INR 1.7 crore. Pro Football Network revenue up 20% with EBITDA margin of 17% (versus -18%). Sportskeeda operating costs down 13% QoQ, with syndication revenue partly offsetting lower ad rates.

segments.name: NODWIN (associate)
segments.commentary: Not reported in the update. H1 revenue and EBITDA are roughly flat; two IPs (I-Popstar and All That Matters) slipped from Q2 to Q3. The Rs 23 crore share of loss in Q2 reflects an EBITDA loss plus an impairment on the Turkish investee Publishme. Pre-IPO round and IPO are being prepared.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue, growth or margin guidance given; management targets 'qualitative' year-on-year growth, organic and inorganic, over the next 3 to 5 years.
Management says margins should be judged on the full year, not one quarter, since August is the seasonally weakest month for mobile gaming.
Fusebox: no timeline for a return to revenue growth; about 7 seasons planned for 2026, with 4 delivered and 2 live; UA and content spend to step up as Traitors metrics allow.
Datawrkz: temporary dip in H2 FY27 as an anchor client pauses ad spend.
NODWIN: growth expected in coming quarters as delayed IPs move into Q3; pre-IPO round and IPO under preparation.
Non-gaming assets (NODWIN, AdTech, Absolute Sports and others) to be monetised opportunistically; management says there is no distressed-sale or hard timeline.

Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition: balance of about $218 million (of $303 million total, $85.5 million paid) payable in three tranches, with roughly $100 million of debt planned and the rest from internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition valued at about $303 million; $85.5 million paid so far, including $77 million funded by a share issuance for the October tranche.
Remaining payments in three tranches: October 2026, then two between December 2026 and March 2027. About $100 million to be raised as debt, with the balance from internal accruals.
Bluetile core capabilities (marketing, data, products, tech) now run as group centres of excellence; a new ad monetisation COE is planned.
Funky Monkeys: 10 new stores in the last 12 months and 5 more planned in FY27.
SMAAASH 2.0 design and rebranding complete; launch slightly delayed pending regulatory approvals and now expected in the next few months.
Wildoku, a Bluetile and BestPlay game launched about 2 to 3 weeks before the call, is under technical testing; several more releases are planned in the ecosystem over the next year.
demand_pricing: Bluetile and BestPlay revenue is about 95% to 96% in-app advertising and the rest in-app purchases; this mix will shift as more IAP-heavy games launch.

Mobile user acquisition and advertising spend was moderated in August-September (about 75% of revenue per the analyst, versus about 85% in Q1 FY27). Management said spend is adjusted for seasonality and is used to build future cohorts.
Kiddopia: subscribers at 5% and ARPU at $7.94 (up 8%); user acquisition stepped up, weighing on EBITDA.

WildWorks: Kitsune content drove the highest daily revenue in the game's lifetime. The Roblox title Animal Jam was shelved after traction missed the bar. Go Slinky Go! soft-launch retention is below threshold, with iterations under way through October and November.
Traitors (Fusebox): early cohorts are described as the most loyal, from existing games, with payer retention above Love Island; management cited a multiple of 2x to 3x Love Island's early metrics.
Sportskeeda: lower ad rates, partly offset by content syndication partnerships launched in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is management's one-year focus under the new CEO, and will flagship launches come or will the focus be on existing games?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on the Nazara platform: moving Bluetile COE leaders into Nazara, adding an ad monetisation COE later, introducing AI across studios, and aiming for an AI-operated group in a year. Gaming remains the main focus, with both iteration of existing games and new launches.

qa_highlights.question: What 5-year growth target is set, e.g. 25% or 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical target given. Management said the goal is 'qualitative' growth, consistently over 5 years, organic at studio level and inorganic at central level via M&A.

qa_highlights.question: Why has NODWIN numerical disclosure stopped and why is offline gaming no longer broken out?
qa_highlights.answer: NODWIN is excluded as gaming is the focus; H1 revenue and EBITDA are almost flat, with I-Popstar and All That Matters slipping to Q3. Offline is to be run as one unit with Funky Monkeys and SMAAASH, and gaming segments will be reported consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: When will Fusebox return to revenue growth, and how do Traitors cohorts monetise versus Love Island?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline given. Traitors early cohorts are the most loyal, with payer retention ahead of Love Island; management cited 2x, then corrected to 3x Love Island's early metrics. About 7 seasons planned for 2026, with 4 delivered and 2 live; UA and content spend to step up.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bluetile and BestPlay revenue grow at lower user acquisition intensity, and what margin and spend ratio should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give guidance. It said August is seasonally the weakest month, margins should be judged annually, and UA spend builds future cohorts. It aims for year-on-year growth over the next few years, with no specific numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-4 year revenue framework and the share of growth from M&A versus organic?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical framework was given. Management reiterated qualitative organic and inorganic growth, and said it is not aggressively pursuing M&A now beyond Bluetile integration, while reviewing opportunities consistently.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR 23 crore share of associate loss, and what is the NODWIN fundraising and IPO timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The loss is entirely NODWIN: an operating EBITDA loss plus a one-time impairment on Turkish investee Publishme. NODWIN is preparing a pre-IPO round and IPO, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition ($303 million) being paid and funded?
qa_highlights.answer: $85.5 million paid so far, with $77 million for the October tranche funded by a share issuance. The balance (about $218 million) is due in three tranches, with about $100 million to be raised as debt and the rest from internal accruals.

risks_watch: Bluetile and BestPlay margin sustainability: Aug-Sep margin of about 19.5% came with lower UA spend (about 75% of revenue vs 85% in Q1 FY27); management says quarterly margins are seasonal and should not be anchored on.
Debt funding: about $100 million of debt still to be raised for the Dec 2026 to Mar 2027 tranches; terms not yet disclosed.
Fusebox revenue down 4% YoY with no timeline for return to growth; Traitors success still early and depends on UA scale-up.
Go Slinky Go! soft-launch retention below threshold and Roblox title Animal Jam shelved; new-title pipeline execution risk.
AdTech: temporary H2 FY27 revenue dip as an anchor client pauses ad spend; EBITDA only INR 0.8 crore in Q2.
NODWIN: H1 flat, two IPs slipped to Q3; pre-IPO round and IPO timing undefined; Publishme impairment in the associate line.
Non-core divestments (NODWIN, AdTech, Absolute Sports and others) have no timeline; management said there is no hard deadline.
key_quotes: Q2 was a record quarter for us: Revenue was INR 803 crores, our highest ever, up 53% year-on-year.
We are not giving exact guidance right now.
So, essentially, August is pretty much the worst month in the year.
But, ultimately, always with one thing in mind, which is qualitative growth.
It is not a distressed sale or anything or a hard timeline that we are committed internally to.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the platform and the gaming pivot, but notably cautious on numbers: management repeatedly declined to give revenue, growth, margin or divestment timelines, and framed growth only as 'qualitative'. Answers on Fusebox timing, NODWIN and the Bluetile margin drop were largely deferred or reframed around seasonality.
